scope: Pixel-carried neural graph, model and current state; generic dual interpreter; refresh continuation

findings.finding: Neural helper functions relied on caller validation and admitted malformed shapes or nonfinite model values.
findings.fix: Validate state, one-to-nine finite model weights, scalar bounds, operator registers/arity, tensor shapes and resource limits.

findings.finding: Checkpoint restore silently converted non-255 pixels to zero and lacked integrity binding of state and model.
findings.fix: Use a bounded integrity manifest covering TIFF state, JSON model and executable graph; validate binary pixels and generic program/model admission.

findings.finding: Input carrier import validated only its first frame, leaving conflicting or corrupted later frames unexamined.
findings.fix: Inspect every frame within explicit byte, dimension, frame and decoded-pixel limits and require one identical job.

findings.finding: Direct sigmoid evaluation could overflow on extreme finite inputs.
findings.fix: Clip finite logits to [-60, 60] before exponentiation while keeping binary classification threshold unchanged.

findings.finding: Output writes could replace existing artifacts and published partial output before all checks passed.
findings.fix: Require a new output directory, retain a stable source-byte snapshot, stage execution, and publish only after numerical and carrier checks pass.

findings.finding: Receipts exposed absolute machine paths and the demo depended on a shared multi-operation application.
findings.fix: Isolate neural-only code and CLI, use Pillow's portable font, and store only relative source paths in evidence.

findings.finding: Windows TemporaryDirectory staging retained an owner-only ACL after publish, preventing desktop-user access.
findings.fix: Use UUID-named ordinary mkdir staging with inherited output permissions, and restored inheritance on existing demo files.

findings.finding: The earlier carrier selected a Python-coded OR recipe instead of carrying the executable graph, model and current state.
findings.fix: Encode the operator graph, weights/bias and state in pixels. Generic tensor and independent scalar interpreters execute that graph. Refreshed carriers advance the saved field. OR/AND model and center-only graph changes produce different outputs from the same host.

findings.finding: Direct scalar reference calls did not bound intermediate integer growth or validate returned grids independently of the primary interpreter.
findings.fix: Check reference intermediate shape/range after every instruction and reject nonbinary outputs or mismatched DOT inputs. Carrier execution already ran the bounded primary interpreter first.

limitations: Generic bounded tensor graph, not an arbitrary-program or full Penteract runtime
Graph/model/state are in pixels; generic Python/NumPy interpreter implementation remains external

Diagnostic probabilities are recalculated from the current binary field
